title: Revit governed graphics control and override state
test_intent: Determine whether applicable Revit category and subcategory graphics resolve through the governed graphics-control hierarchy and whether recurring display behavior, subcategory use, and exceptions remain free of unexplained local drift.

applicability.applies_when: The tested Revit model, template, family, or documentation scope contains category/subcategory graphics governed through Object Styles, view templates, rule-based filters, materials, or approved subcategory definitions.
applicability.not_applicable_when: The tested scope contains no Revit category/subcategory graphics subject to a governed graphics-control rule.

required_evidence: applicable governed graphics-control configuration or registry entries
observed Object Styles and applicable category/subcategory graphics state
applicable view-template and rule-based filter graphics state
inventory of recurring local view or element overrides within the tested scope
inventory of applicable family/detail subcategories and their governed identities
record of approved graphics exceptions where applicable

result_logic.pass: Every applicable graphics condition resolves through the approved control layer or an approved traceable exception; recurring display logic is reproducible through governed Object Styles, templates, filters, materials, or approved subcategories; and no unexplained local drift or unapproved subcategory proliferation is present.
result_logic.fail: An applicable graphics condition conflicts with an available governed rule, depends on an unexplained recurring local override, introduces an unapproved duplicate or near-duplicate subcategory, or bypasses an available governed control layer without an approved traceable exception.
result_logic.not_applicable: No graphics condition in the tested scope is subject to a governed graphics-control rule.
result_logic.indeterminate: The applicable governed graphics configuration, expected category/subcategory definition, display context, or exception record is unavailable or incomplete, so conformance cannot be determined without inventing expected values.

provenance.migration_note: Appendix E ATS for governed Revit graphics-control conformance. Source example line weights, colors, hatch names, subcategory names, and other unconfirmed numeric or office-specific values remain noncanonical; absence of governed expected values produces an indeterminate result rather than invented authority.
